neighbours.label: a 'That' or ', which' whose referent is the whole preceding statement (That's the key; ..., which was a good thing), as against 'that'/'which' as a determiner, a restrictive relative, or a relative tied to a single noun
fire: Get plenty of sleep before the exam. That's the single most important tip.
We cooked dinner together every night of the trip. That was what I loved most.
The baby started sleeping through the night, which was a huge relief for us.
My grandfather walked five miles every morning. That's how he stayed healthy.
The company cut its prices by half, which surprised nearly every analyst.
Keep your eyes on the ball and swing smoothly. That's all there is to it.
She stopped checking her phone at dinner, which made the evenings much calmer.
Spend an hour outside with your kids each day. That's the best gift you can give.
quiet: Before the exam, that tip about sleep is the one I remember most.
We cooked the dinner that my aunt had taught us during the trip.
The baby, which my sister adopted, sleeps through the night now.
My grandfather rode that old bicycle five miles every morning.
The company cut the prices that customers had complained about.
The ball in that garage belongs to the boy next door.
She kept the phone, which was a gift from her father, in a drawer.
Spend the hour that you save each day outside with your kids.

predictions: fire 0.3-0.85 on statement-referring That/which; determiner, restrictive and noun-attached relatives below 0.15
